summary.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crores; consolidated INR299 crores (+18% YoY), with order book at ~INR4,500 crores.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crores and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crores (+18% YoY), but both fell sequentially as new projects were at early execution stage and older projects that had delivered Q1 savings rolled off. Management attributed the lower Q2 margin to project mix, upfront costs on new orders, organisation-building costs and one-time consolidation costs after the group restructuring. Orders of about INR1,200 crores were won in the quarter, lifting the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crores as of June 2026, of which standalone is about INR2,200 crores. Management expects revenue and margin to build in H2 as new projects ramp.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue (Q1 CY26, as restated, per analyst)

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR149 crores, up 82% YoY; top customers Tata Steel and JSW. Standalone order book ~INR2,200 crores.

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR299 crores, up 18% YoY; ArcelorMittal to be added to top customers. Top five customers ~80% of revenue. Consolidated order book ~INR4,500 crores.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Q2 service revenue about one-third of Q1 level, attributed to slower project progress rather than lack of orders; management says service margins remain strong and backlog is good.

guidance_outlook: INR8,000 crores top-line remains the north-star target by CY30, to come from organic growth (JVD, Volteron) plus external acquisitions that management is evaluating.
Management expects significant revenue improvement in H2 CY26, though it said the company may not reach the ~INR2,000 crores CY25 consolidated revenue level previously guided, even including the US.
Engineering is in progress on new projects; execution ramp-up in H2 is planned, with impact depending on engineering and procurement before year-end.
Standard contract execution timeline is 2-3 years; management assumes three years for current order book.
Employee costs expected to rise modestly due to execution-side hiring; other expenses expected marginally lower over next two quarters.
Parent-level share-based payment arrangement expected to end transaction-related costs from H2 CY26.
Further order wins expected before year-end across Asia, Europe, US and India; a JVD contract in Asia targeted this year; a cold rolling order of EUR50-100 million expected.
capex_capacity: Advanced Coating facility inaugurated at Taloja, India; management said the Taloja Rolls Coating facility was put into operation in June, with trial orders and production initiation underway.
New Shanghai office opened in China; a workshop in China planned to open in Q3 CY26 for assembly of special machines and equipment.
Management said capacity expansion is needed on the execution side, with manpower additions planned.
Preferential convertible share issue to John Cockerill SA planned, which management said would take its stake back above 72%.
demand_pricing: Strong order inflow of ~INR1,200 crores in the quarter; management cites healthy inquiries and demand for advanced processing, electrical steel, downstream quality and plant modernisation.
Europe: EU tariff-quota regime from July 2026 covering 18.3 million tonnes, 15% duty on out-of-quota imports; slabs exempt, supporting hot-rolling, cold-rolling and processing-line demand.
US: capacity utilisation 82% in July 2026, highest since 2018; producers to invest over USD14 billion this year.
India: steel production expected at 161.7 million tonnes this year; target 300 million tonnes by 2030; per-capita consumption ~93 kg vs global ~230 kg.
JVD (Jet Vapor Deposition) customer decision delayed as customer's investment-approval process is longer than expected; management says other cases are under discussion.
Competition named as SMS and Danieli (Tier 1 OEMs); management said all competitors have downstream portfolios. Management declined to name a main Indian competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crores top-line target by CY30 still valid, and how will it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it the north star, with organic growth from JVD and Volteron plus external acquisitions being evaluated. JVD is commercial with an advanced Asia discussion targeted this year; Volteron is not yet commercial and IP sits with John Cockerill SA.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gap between the ~INR2,000 crores CY25 guidance and reported ~INR960 crores explained, and would the US entity bridge it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR2,000 crores was a guideline, the US is not a large contributor, and revenue depends on project progress. It expects a significant H2 improvement and said it may not reach INR2,000 crores but should not be far off, even including the US.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce its stake from 75% to ~70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent has portfolio priorities and periodically adjusts holdings; it remains a large shareholder, and a preferential convertible issue would take its stake back above 72%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical JVD cost differential versus hot-dip galvanising and the typical order size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined precise cost figures, saying it depends on product mix; savings to customers are at least INR1,000 and up to 20x that per case, mainly from avoiding batch annealing for automotive and AHSS. The cold rolling order under discussion is EUR50-100 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost may rise modestly from hiring on the execution side; other expenses may be marginally lower than Q2 (~INR70 crores) over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What were the service revenue, top customer and regional split figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Service revenue in Q2 was about one-third of Q1 level, reflecting slower project progress rather than order loss. Top customers are Tata Steel and JSW (standalone), with ArcelorMittal added on a consolidated basis; top five are ~80% of revenue. Regional split was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off and ongoing consolidation costs, and how long will they last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs include transaction, forex and notional interest impacts plus legal, audit and compliance costs across Belgium, Germany and China. The parent agreed to a share-based payment instead of cash, so these costs should stop from H2. It could not quantify Q2 costs and said it would follow up.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in H2, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said engineering is in progress and ramp-up depends on engineering and procurement before year-end, impacting H2. Contract durations are typically 2-3 years, with three years assumed for current projects. Margins were described as consistent to slightly improving, with H2 mix expected to help as value-added services contribute more.

risks_watch: Execution ramp-up in H2 depends on engineering and procurement completed before year-end; Q2 revenue and margin fell sequentially as new projects were in early stage.
Management said the ~INR2,000 crores CY25 consolidated guideline may not be reached; reported ~INR960 crores figure cited by analyst was not confirmed by management.

Consolidation and transaction costs (forex, notional interest, legal, audit, compliance across Belgium, Germany, China) were not quantified for Q2; management will follow up and says parent share-based payment should stop costs from H2 CY26.
JVD first contract delayed as customer investment-approval process is longer than expected; Volteron is not commercial and its IP sits with John Cockerill SA.
Employee cost expected to rise on execution-side hiring; other expenses expected only marginally lower over next two quarters.
Service revenue fell to about one-third of Q1 level; management attributes this to slower project progress and says service backlog and margins remain strong.
Parent John Cockerill SA stake reduced from 75% to about 70.4%; planned preferential convertible issue would take it above 72%, pending completion.
key_quotes: Revenue was lower on a sequential basis. This was mainly due to the project cycle and the timing of revenue recognition.
We secured order worth approximately INR1,200 crores. With these wins, our total order book as of June 2026 stands at approximately INR4,500 crores.

So, I think you will see a significant improvement in the revenue generation. In the second half and I think, okay, we may not be at 2,000, but I think we should not be very far if at all we include the U.S. in that.
Fortunately, the parent company has agreed to go for a share -based payment instead of a cash payment.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on order inflow, demand trends and H2 recovery, but cautious and partly evasive on the numbers: it declined to quantify consolidation costs, JVD cost differentials, regional split and the top-customer share, and it did not confirm the CY25 revenue gap. Audio problems also interrupted parts of the Q&A.
